finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST handler passes the user-supplied 'feed' value straight to file_get_contents(). The attacker controls scheme and host, so they can make the server request internal hosts, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), or other URL-wrapper targets such as ftp:// and file://. The response is not returned, but strlen($xml) is echoed. That gives a size oracle, port-scan and timing signals, and blind SSRF. The default allow_url_fopen=On is assumed. Redirects are followed by the http wrapper. Severity is HIGH because there is no auth and no allowlist.

trace.note: Only checks REQUEST_METHOD === 'POST' and isset($_POST['feed']); no require_admin() call
$xml = file_get_contents($_POST['feed']); the URL is used directly with no parsing or transformation
echo strlen($xml) returns the fetched body length to the attacker (size/reachability oracle)

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme restriction, hostname check, or IP/CIDR block. The only auth helper, require_admin() (lines 4-9), is not called on this path, so any caller (session or not) reaches the sink. Redirects are not disabled. No in-repo egress controls.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes $_POST['feed'] directly to file_get_contents() and echoes strlen($xml), with no require_admin() call (it is defined at lines 4-9 but only used at line 18) and no host or scheme validation.
